result:
`bridge.npz` is saved in your folder, with M of shape 64 × 96 and c of shape 96. On my own held-out Python text the bridged model got **63.9%** next-character accuracy. B alone got 71.8% on that same text, so the bridge loses about 8 points.

That 63.9% is not a prediction of your score. My held-out text is easier than your test text, since B alone scores 72% on it but about 63% on yours. If the same loss carries over, expect roughly 55–58% on your text. I also picked the saved bridge by its score on this same held-out set, so the 63.9% is slightly optimistic.

**How it was built:**
1. **Forward pass:** I implemented both models in numpy and checked them on Python text I wrote myself. A and B scored 73% and 73% on my hand-written code, and about 65% on generated code.
2. **First attempt:** I fitted M and c by least squares, so that A's block-2 residual mapped onto B's block-2 residual at every position. This explained only 57% of B's residual variance and gave 43.7% accuracy.
3. **Training on B's outputs:** I wrote backpropagation through B's blocks 2 and 3, final norm and head, and checked it against numerical gradients. I then trained M and c with Adam so that B's predictions through the bridge match B's own predictions. Accuracy rose to about 60.5%.
4. **More training text:** The rule against reading outside files left me only text I wrote myself, about 6 KB plus a generated set of random Python-like functions. I added about 5,100 64-character windows sampled from B and from A themselves. This brought the bridge to 63.9%. A final round with a decaying learning rate did not improve it further.
